stem.text: In an experiment, pieces of onion epidermis are put into three different concentrations of sucrose solutions, P, Q and R. The pieces of onion are left for an hour and then examined using the low power of a light microscope.
Each diagram shows one cell from the epidermis that was placed in each of the sucrose concentrations.

stem.label: P
stem.alt: Outline of a plant cell with a large central region, a dark dot near the edge and a thin outer layer, labelled P.

stem.label: Q
stem.alt: Outline of a plant cell with a large central region, a dark dot at the left end and a thin outer layer, labelled Q.

stem.label: R
stem.alt: Outline of a plant cell with an irregular central region, a dark dot and a small oval, labelled R.

stem.text: What explains the appearance of cells in solution Q?

A.text: The concentration of solution Q is equal to the concentration of the solutes in the cell sap.

B.text: The cytoplasm has the same concentration of sucrose as solution Q.

C.text: The water potential of the cytoplasm is equal to the water potential of the vacuole.

D.text: The water potential of the cell sap is equal to the water potential of solution Q.
